sources.citation: Daigle, Benjamin T. 2015. A grammar sketch of Batuley: An Austronesian language of Aru, eastern Indonesia. MA thesis, Leiden University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Describes Batuley, not Barakai. Mentions Barakai only for classification (Batuley relatively close to the Barakai-Karey grouping, citing Hughes 1987: 95); its survey of previous work on Aru languages (sec. 1.2, fn. 18) lists no description of Barakai.

sources.citation: Hughes, Jock. 1987. The languages of Kei, Tanimbar and Aru: Lexicostatistic classification. In Soenjono Dardjowidjojo (ed.), Miscellaneous studies of Indonesian and other languages in Indonesia, part 9 (NUSA 27), 71-111. Jakarta: Universitas Katolik Indonesia Atma Jaya.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Image-only scan, scanned. Sec. 2.2.3.11 'Barakai' gives location (Barakai Island + Gomo-Gomo), >2,400 speakers, two dialects (Mesiang vs. Longgar/Apara/Bemun/Gomo-Gomo, 87% cognate) and vitality; classification places Barakai with Karey. No stress/accent/syllable statements anywhere in the article.
